claim: Untrusted OAuth `expires_in` (u64) is cast to i64 and added to the current time without saturation, so extreme provider values wrap the stored token expiry into the past and force repeated refreshes (or an overflow panic in debug builds).
evidence: crates/mehh-mcp/src/oauth.rs:50-51 `pub fn mcp_token_expiry_seconds(expires_in: u64) -> i64 { (mehh_ai::now_ms() / 1000) + expires_in as i64 }` and :1224 `let expire_at = new_tokens.expires_in.map(|exp| now + exp as i64);`. `OAuthTokens.expires_in` (:40) is deserialized directly from the token endpoint JSON at :1126 and at crates/mehh-coding-agent/src/mcp_manager.rs:520-529 with no bound check. The sibling implementation in crates/mehh-ai/src/oauth.rs:169-173 deliberately uses saturating_mul/saturating_add 'saturating instead of overflowing on hostile provider values'.
runtimeTrigger: A configured MCP OAuth token endpoint returns {"access_token":"a","expires_in":18446744073709551615}. `exp as i64` becomes -1, so tokens_expire_at = now-1. On the next bearer_token() call, :1252 sees exp <= now+30, enters the refresh path, the server returns the same value, and every subsequent request performs another refresh instead of reusing a live token.
